Name: MAPS_Compression
Label: MAPS compression
Note: AEMO 2025 Gas Infrastructure Options Report, Appendix A2: "Moomba Adelaide Pipeline System to Port Campbell to Adelaide pipeline connection" -- "Dedicated connection from MAPS to PCA" plus "Compression", source "Gas Infrastructure Options Report consultation", zone Southern, capacity "Not published". THIS ROW IS THE COMPRESSION HALF ONLY. The dedicated MAPS-to-PCA connection is already implicit in GARY's topology -- the Adelaide node is where the MAPS meets SEA_Gas_Rev -- so a candidate for it would model nothing; the compression is the half that moves a number. SIZING IS A PUBLISHED ENDPOINT, NOT A GARY GUESS: the SA Department for Energy and Mining's petroleum infrastructure page gives the mainline's fully compressed capacity, with all seven compressor stations online, as ~110 PJ/yr, against ~91 PJ/yr in its current four-station configuration. 91 PJ/yr is 249 TJ/d, which is exactly the AEMC pipeline register's rating and GARY's MAPS arc, so the two figures sit on one basis and the increment follows: 110 PJ/yr = 301 TJ/d, less the 249 base = 52 TJ/d. It is conservative against the pipe's own history -- Epic Energy's NCC coverage-revocation application put the system's firm capacity at 348 TJ/d as configured in December 2004 and its maximum at 418 TJ/d. CAPEX IS GARY'S OWN, at the SWP compression unit rate ($213m AER-approved for 45 TJ/d = $4.73m per TJ/d), the closest analogue in the model: new compression on an existing southern transmission line. It is deliberately the DEAR end of the range, because the seven MAPS stations already exist and four of them run, so recommissioning should cost less than greenfield units -- and a candidate that relieves the largest congestion rent in the model should not also be flattered on price. EARLIEST YEAR IS A GARY CONVENTION, NOT A PUBLISHED DATE: AEMO's options report gives none, and 2029 matches the other proposed southern projects rather than letting a consultation-stage option be built next year.

Name: NGP_Reversal
Label: NGP reversal
Note: Reverse-flow service on Jemena's Northern Gas Pipeline, so southern gas can reach the NT. WHY THIS EXISTS AT ALL: NGP_Rev previously sat in arcs.csv as an EXISTING arc at 106 TJ/d, free from day one, and carried 16,107 TJ north over the horizon in the central case (157,000 in LNG Low). Two things were wrong with that. The 106 is the GSOO's figure for the NGP, which describes gas leaving the NT, and it had been applied to the arc bringing gas in. And the service is not offered: the GBB rates Mt Isa -> Tennant Creek at 60 TJ/d NAMEPLATE but publishes 0.000 for it across the whole medium-term outlook (2026-06-04 to 2028-06-03), 0.000 every day of the short-term outlook and 0.000 uncontracted every month, while the forward direction runs at 80-90. A physical rating that is not sold is a project, not an existing arc -- which is how EGP_Rev, SEA_Gas_Rev, Bulloo and NEAP are all already handled. CAPACITY IS THE GBB NAMEPLATE, 60 TJ/d, not the 106 that was there. CAPEX IS GARY'S OWN at the EGP reversal unit rate ($220m / 200 TJ/d = $1.11m per TJ/d), the closest analogue in the model: reversing an existing long-haul pipeline, and Jemena's in both cases. EARLIEST YEAR IS A GARY CONVENTION, not a published date -- AEMO publishes no reversal project for the NGP at all, so this candidate is GARY's own reading of what the 60 TJ/d nameplate would cost to make available.
